newsitem.title: USA: LDC DEBT PRICES BOOSTED BY RISING U.S. TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: LDC DEBT PRICES BOOSTED BY RISING U.S. TREASURIES.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were quoted about 3/4 of a point higher on Tuesday, boosted by rising U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
"The market was boosted by Treasuries... People are viewing this market as still yield attractive," said one trader.
Traders said volume was heavy with players keying in on the upcoming supply of new debt, traders said.
Argentine bonds were boosted by Tuesday's successful launch of the country's 10-year global bond via joint lead managers Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
"The Argentina deal was a blowout in London...it met with overwhelming demand," said one corporate high-grade syndicate source in New York.
After meeting with overwhelming investor demand, Argentina increased the size of its global bond issue to 1.0 billion from an initial 750 million, the Argentine Economic Ministry said on Tuesday.

"Even though the initial amount was for 750 million, the excellent response that this issue had in the international financial community brought us to increase the issue to 1.0 billion," the ministry said in a statement.
The 10-year bonds will be placed at between 445-450 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note and is expected to price on Wednesday, the ministry said.
Meanwhile, Bear Stearns & Co Inc is expected to underwrite a deal via a private placement offering for the billionaire Dart family, market sources said.
Bear Stearns was unavailable for comment.
The deal would represent the last existing Multi-Year Deposit Facility Agreement (MYDFA) loans not subject to the Brady bond restructuring, the sources added.

"Prior to 1994, everyone owned MYDFAs and the Dart family did not convert, making them one of the last owners of the Brazilian debt," said Thomas Trebat, managing director of emerging market research at Citicorp Securities.
Brazil reached a debt restructuring agreement earlier in this year with the Dart family, holders of about 1.3 billion in sovereign debt, not included in a 1994 Brady accord.
The deal is expected to be priced on Wednesday and consists of about 1.3 billion in MYDFA Trust Certificates due 2007, sources said.
The certificates are expected to be issued at a discount with price talk seen at 110-120 basis points over the Brazilian EI bonds, sources added.
"The reason why they're comparing spreads to EI's (bonds) is because they have a similar structure," said Denis Parisien, an analyst at I.D.E.A Inc.
Meanwhile, Brazil is also expected to tap the market with a 750 million global deal of its own. The offering is expected to consist of a five or 10-year maturity, dealers said.
Price talk on a potential five-year issue is seen around 250 basis points over Treasuries, although some traders said the low 200s was possible.
In the Brady bond market, Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR were up 7/8 at 59-1/4 bid, while Argentine FRBs ARFLCO5=RR were up 5/8 at 84-3/8.

Meanwhile, Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR were up 3/4 to trade at 71-1/8 bid and Brazilian Pars BR4D24=RR were up 1/2 at 60 bid. In other issues, Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper RUVNUSLNS=RR gained 1-5/8 to end the trading day at 71-1/4 bid.

Looking ahead players are expected to key in on Friday's release of September U.S. nonfarm payrolls and unemployment by the Labor Department.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists expect September nonfarm payroll to increase by 166,000 and for unemployment to rise slightly to a 5.2 percent rate.
